concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: After the decisive battle of Plassey of 1757, who among the following was declared as the Nawab of Bengal by the British?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Mir Jafar Ali Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After the **Battle of Plassey** in **1757**, the British East India Company defeated the forces of **Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah**, marking a decisive turning point in Indian history.
 
• **Mir Jafar Ali Khan**, a former commander in Siraj ud-Daulah’s army, was installed as the **Nawab of Bengal** by the British as a reward for his betrayal during the battle.
 
• Mir Jafar’s installation allowed the British East India Company to gain significant control over **Bengal’s administration and resources**.
 
• The battle and Mir Jafar’s subsequent appointment marked the beginning of the **British political and economic dominance** in India.
 
• Mir Jafar is often regarded as the first puppet ruler in Indian history, as his governance was heavily influenced by the British.
 
• The British exploited Mir Jafar’s position to expand their influence and strengthen their control over **Bengal’s wealth and trade**.
 
• The events following Mir Jafar’s appointment demonstrated the **British strategy of installing rulers who were dependent on their support**, a tactic they continued to use across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mir Qasim**__

 __
 
• **Mir Qasim** was later appointed as the Nawab of Bengal by the British after Mir Jafar, but he rebelled against British interference in his administration.
 
• Mir Qasim moved his capital from **Murshidabad to Monghyr** to establish independence from British control.
 
• His conflict with the British led to the **Battle of Buxar in 1764**, where the British emerged victorious.
 
 
 
• **Mansur Ali Khan**__
 __
 
• **Mansur Ali Khan**, also known as **Wajid Ali Shah**, was the Nawab of Awadh, not Bengal.
 
• He is known for his patronage of **music, dance, and arts**, rather than for significant political events in Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Murshid Quli Khan**__
 
 
• **Murshid Quli Khan** was the first Nawab of Bengal, long before the Battle of Plassey, and he established **Murshidabad** as the capital of Bengal.
 
• He was known for his administrative reforms and efficient tax collection system.
